parts.gloss: one who does not see or know

words.gloss: one who does not know (an ignorant person)

parts.gloss: he who tries to show or teach
one who does not see or know
becomes or is said to be
that which was seen or understood

literal: He who instructs an ignorant person himself does not see; the ignorant person becomes one who has understood only in the way he himself understands.
translation: One who attempts to instruct an ignorant person is himself devoid of wisdom; and that ignorant person will only claim to have understood in his own limited, distorted way.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவனுக்கு அறிவுறுத்த முயல்பவன் தானும் அறிவில்லாதவன் ஆவான்; அந்த அறிவில்லாதவனோ தான் புரிந்து கொண்ட வழியிலேயே புரிந்து கொண்டதாகக் கொள்வான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of trying to teach someone who lacks the capacity or willingness to understand. The poet states that a person who attempts to instruct an ignorant person (காணாதான்) is himself acting without wisdom (தான் காணான்), as it is a pointless endeavor. Furthermore, the ignorant person will not grasp the true meaning of the instruction; instead, they will only interpret and believe they have understood it (கண்டானாம்) in their own flawed and limited way (தான் கண்ட ஆறு). Thus, true knowledge cannot be forced upon those who are unprepared to receive it.
